description: Reusable .NET 10 package that wraps ASP.NET Core Identity with cookie and JWT auth, Google OAuth, a pluggable e-mail provider, a multi-tenant model with dynamic RBAC (roles + module permissions), and secure defaults — wired up with a single AddMyIdentity call. JWT and Google OAuth secrets are supplied by the consumer (never shipped in the package).
releaseNotes: v5.6.0:a Blazor Server circuit ends with its cookie, a user can change their own password without losing the session, and the first SystemAdmin can be created inside a tenant. Behaviour change (security): MyIdentityRevalidatingAuthenticationStateProvider now answers anonymous, and notifies subscribers, once the ExpiresUtc of the cookie ticket that opened the circuit passes, with no wait for RevalidationIntervalMinutes; activity in the circuit does not renew it, so size ExpireTimeSpan for how long a user stays on one page; the cut is measured over WebSockets, and over long polling the provider already starts anonymous. Behaviour change (security): inside a Blazor Server circuit, also in a scope the application opens in it (OwningComponentBase, IServiceScopeFactory) during each inbound activity of the circuit, IMyIdentityCurrentUserAccessor, and so every gate of the library, reads the circuit's state instead of the HttpContext.User of the request that opened the circuit, which over WebSockets stayed frozen past the cookie's expiry and past a rotated security stamp; a request outside a circuit still reads HttpContext.User, and a MyIdentityCompositeCurrentUserAccessor built by hand keeps the earlier rule. Behaviour change (security): with the SignInManager AddMyIdentity registers, the second step of Identity's two-factor sign-in refuses an account that is deleted or disabled, must change its password, or whose tenant does not resolve or is inactive, before the code is checked, and the cookie ends with an account disabled or deleted even when nothing rotated the security stamp; a Blazor Server circuit drops a SystemAdmin or TenantAdmin role the store no longer gives. New MyIdentity:Authentication:Cookies:CookieExpireTimeSpanMinutes (no default) wins over CookieExpireTimeSpanDays when greater than 0. New IMyIdentityAuthenticationService.ChangeOwnPasswordAsync changes the password of the account the application cookie belongs to and re-signs that session with the new security stamp (other sessions end; call it from an endpoint, not a circuit). New IMyIdentityUserService.RequirePasswordChangeAsync sets MustChangePassword and rotates the stamp, in the unit of work in the flow; an account without a password is refused with the new MyIdentityErrorCodes.UserHasNoPassword. New IMyIdentityBootstrapService.CreateFirstSystemAdminAsync overload takes a tenant id and creates the first SystemAdmin in that existing, active tenant, with TenantAdmin. New MyIdentityLockout.GetState tells an administrator's lock from a lock-out by failed attempts, from LockoutEnd alone. New IMyIdentityPermissionAdminService.GetUserRoleAssignmentsForUserAsync lists the role assignments of one user, filtered in the database, with the gate of GetUserRoleAssignmentsAsync (a TenantAdmin asking for a user outside their tenant, or one that does not exist, gets PermissionDenied). MyIdentityModuleDefinition gains Name and Description, and the startup seed now updates a module row's declared texts (behaviour change); a platform module that declares one fails startup. Breaking: a hand-written IMyIdentityAuthenticationService, IMyIdentityUserService, IMyIdentityBootstrapService or IMyIdentityPermissionAdminService adds one member each; CreateFirstSystemAdminAsync and AddModule each gained an overload, so a method group of either whose delegate type the compiler infers (var f = bootstrap.CreateFirstSystemAdminAsync;) no longer compiles (CS8917); every call compiles as before; a localized MyIdentityMessageDescriber overrides CannotRequirePasswordChangeWithoutPassword. The Microsoft packages move to 10.0.14. The package validation baseline is 5.5.0. Upgrading from 5.5.0: MyIdentity/UPGRADE.md §50.
